title_en: Notice of the Ministry of Emergency Management, the Ministry of Public Security, the Supreme People's Court, and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Issuing the Measures for the Connection between Administrative Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice in Work Safety
full_text_en:
Ministry of Emergency Management, Ministry of Public Security, Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Notice on the Issuance of the "Work Measures for the Connection between Administrative Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice in Work Safety"

Emergency [2019] No. 54

To the departments (bureaus) of emergency management, public security departments (bureaus), higher people's courts, and people's procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Emergency Management Bureau, Public Security Bureau, Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and People's Procuratorate of the Production and Construction Corps of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and all provincial-level coal mine safety supervision bureaus:

In order to establish and improve the working mechanism for the connection between administrative law enforcement and criminal justice in work safety, legally punish illegal and criminal acts in work safety, and protect the safety of people's lives and property and social stability, the Ministry of Emergency Management, the Ministry of Public Security, the Supreme People's Court, and the Supreme People's Procuratorate have jointly studied and formulated the "Work Measures for the Connection between Administrative Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice in Work Safety," which are hereby issued for your compliance and implementation.

April 16, 2019

Work Measures for the Connection between Administrative Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice in Work Safety

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Provisions on the Transfer of Suspected Criminal Cases by Administrative Law Enforcement Organs, the Regulations on the Reporting, Investigation and Handling of Production Safety Accidents, the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases Involving Endangering Production Safety, and other laws, administrative regulations, judicial interpretations, and relevant provisions, for the purposes of establishing and improving the working mechanism for the connection between administrative law enforcement and criminal justice in work safety, legally punishing illegal and criminal acts in work safety, and protecting the safety of people's lives and property and social stability.

Article 2 These Measures apply to cases involving suspected work safety crimes handled by emergency management departments, public security organs, people's courts, and people's procuratorates.

Cases involving other suspected crimes discovered by emergency management departments in the course of investigating illegal acts shall be handled by reference to these Measures.

The term "emergency management departments" as used in these Measures includes coal mine safety supervision agencies and fire protection agencies.

These Measures do not apply to cases involving suspected work safety crimes that fall within the scope of the Supervision Law of the People's Republic of China, which are committed by public officials in the exercise of public authority and are subject to investigation by supervisory organs according to law; such cases shall be promptly transferred to supervisory organs for handling according to law.

Article 3 Cases involving suspected work safety crimes mainly include the following types:

(1) Cases of major liability accidents;
(2) Cases of ordering operations in violation of rules and taking risks;
(3) Cases of major labor safety accidents;
(4) Cases of accidents caused by dangerous articles;
(5) Cases of fire liability accidents and arson;
(6) Cases of failing to report or falsely reporting safety accidents;
(7) Other criminal cases involving suspected work safety, such as illegal mining, illegal manufacture, sale, or storage of explosives, illegal business operations, and forgery, alteration, or sale of official documents, certificates, or seals of state organs.

Article 4 People's procuratorates shall exercise legal supervision over the transfer of suspected work safety crime cases by emergency management departments and the filing activities of public security organs in accordance with the law.

Article 5 Emergency management departments, public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts at all levels shall strengthen cooperation, unify the application of law, and continuously improve working mechanisms for case transfer, case notification, and information sharing.

Article 6 If, in the course of administrative law enforcement, an emergency management department discovers clues of a suspected work safety crime committed by a public official exercising public authority, or if, in the course of investigating relevant illegal or criminal acts, an emergency management department, public security organ, or people's procuratorate discovers clues of a public official exercising public authority suspected of engaging in duty-related illegal acts or duty crimes such as embezzlement, bribery, dereliction of duty, or malfeasance, such clues shall be promptly transferred to the supervisory organ for handling according to law.

Chapter II Case Transfer and Legal Supervision in Routine Law Enforcement

Article 7 If, in the course of investigating illegal acts, an emergency management department discovers a case involving a suspected work safety crime, it shall immediately designate two or more administrative law enforcement personnel to form a special case team to take charge, verify the situation, and submit a written report on the transfer of the suspected criminal case. The principal responsible person or the person in charge of the emergency management department shall make a decision to approve or disapprove the transfer within three days from the date of receiving the report. If the transfer is approved, it shall be made to the public security organ at the same level within 24 hours; if the transfer is not approved, the reasons for the disapproval shall be recorded.

Article 8 When transferring a suspected work safety crime case to a public security organ, the emergency management department shall attach the following materials and send a copy of the case transfer letter to the people's procuratorate at the same level:

(1) A case transfer letter, stating the name of the transferring emergency management department, the suspected crime of the illegal act, the name and contact information of the person in charge of the case, etc. The case transfer letter shall be accompanied by a list of transferred materials and be stamped with the official seal of the emergency management department;
(2) A case investigation report, stating the source of the case, the circumstances of the seizure, the basic information of the suspect, the facts of the suspected crime, evidence, legal basis, and handling recommendations, etc.;
(3) A list of items involved in the case, stating the name, quantity, characteristics, storage location, etc., of the items, accompanied by relevant materials indicating the source of the items, such as administrative compulsory measures and on-site records;
(4) An inspection report or expert opinion accompanied by the qualification certificate of the inspection institution and inspector or other supporting documents;
(5) Other evidentiary materials related to the case, such as on-site photos, interrogation records, electronic data, audio-visual materials, identification opinions, and corrective action notices.

If an administrative penalty decision has already been made for the relevant illegal act, the administrative penalty decision shall also be attached.

Article 9 Upon receiving a suspected work safety crime case transferred by an emergency management department, the public security organ shall issue a receipt for acceptance of the case or sign the receipt on the case transfer letter.

Article 10 If, upon review, the public security organ finds that the materials for the transferred suspected work safety crime case are incomplete, it shall inform the emergency management department in writing within 24 hours of receiving the case to make up for the deficiencies within three days.

If, upon review, the public security organ finds that the materials for the transferred suspected work safety crime case are incomplete or the evidence is insufficient, it may propose supplementary investigation opinions on the relevant evidence required to prove the existence of criminal facts, and the transferring emergency management department shall conduct a supplementary investigation. The public security organ may, according to the actual circumstances, conduct its own investigation in accordance with the law.

Article 11 For a transferred suspected work safety crime case, the public security organ shall make a decision on whether to file the case within three days from the date of receiving the case; if the suspected criminal clues require verification, the decision shall be made within seven days from the date of receiving the case; for major, difficult, or complex cases, the decision may be made within 30 days from the date of receiving the case with the approval of the responsible person of the public security organ at or above the county level. If the case is not filed in accordance with the law, reasons shall be given, and the case materials shall be returned accordingly.

For cases that fall within the jurisdiction of the public security organs but not within the jurisdiction of the receiving public security organ, they shall be transferred to the public security organ with jurisdiction within 24 hours of receiving the case, and the transferring emergency management department shall be notified in writing, with a copy sent to the people's procuratorate at the same level. For cases that do not fall within the jurisdiction of the public security organs, they shall be returned to the transferring emergency management department within 24 hours.

Article 12 If a public security organ makes a decision to file or not to file a case, it shall notify the emergency management department in writing within three days from the date of making the decision, and send a copy to the people's procuratorate at the same level.

If a public security organ decides to dismiss a case after filing it for a transferred suspected work safety crime case, it shall serve the decision to dismiss the case on the transferring emergency management department and return the case files. If administrative legal liability should be pursued according to law, written recommendations may also be made at the same time. The decision to dismiss the case shall be copied to the people's procuratorate at the same level.

Article 13 The emergency management department shall transfer the items involved in the case and other materials related to the case to the public security organ within three days from the date of receiving the notice of case filing from the public security organ, and go through the handover procedures.

For items involved in the case that have special requirements for storage conditions and storage locations, after the public security organ takes necessary measures to secure and retain the evidence, the emergency management department may take custody on its behalf. The emergency management department shall properly keep the items involved in the case and cooperate with the public security organ, people's procuratorate, and people's court in the retrieval, use, and appraisal of the items involved in the case during the handling of the case.

Article 14 If an emergency management department, after receiving the notice of non-filing of a case from the public security organ, believes that the case should be filed by the public security organ according to law, it may, within three days from the date of receiving the notice of non-filing, apply for reconsideration to the public security organ that made the non-filing decision, or recommend that the people's procuratorate carry out filing supervision.

The public security organ shall make a reconsideration decision within three days from the date of receiving the application for reconsideration and notify the emergency management department in writing. If the emergency management department still disagrees with the reconsideration decision of the public security organ, it shall, within three days from the date of receiving the reconsideration decision, recommend that the people's procuratorate carry out filing supervision.

If the emergency management department disagrees with the public security organ's failure to make a decision on whether to file a case within the time limit or with the decision to dismiss a case after filing, it may recommend that the people's procuratorate carry out filing supervision.

Article 15 When an emergency management department recommends that a people's procuratorate carry out filing supervision, it shall provide a recommendation letter for filing supervision, relevant case materials, and attach the public security organ's notice of non-filing, the notice of maintaining the non-filing decision upon reconsideration, or the decision to dismiss the case after filing, along with relevant explanations.

Article 16 The people's procuratorate shall review the recommendation for filing supervision from the emergency management department. If it considers it necessary for the public security organ to explain the reasons for not filing the case or for dismissing the case after filing, it shall require the public security organ to provide explanations within seven days. The public security organ shall provide written explanations and reply to the people's procuratorate.

If, upon review, the people's procuratorate considers that the public security organ's reasons for not filing the case or dismissing the case after filing are sufficient and conform to the legal circumstances, it shall issue a prosecutorial opinion supporting the non-filing or dismissal of the case. If it considers that the relevant reasons are not valid, it shall notify the public security organ to file the case.

After receiving the notice of case filing, the public security organ shall file the case within 15 days and serve the decision to file the case on the people's procuratorate.

Article 17 If a people's procuratorate discovers that an emergency management department has not transferred a suspected work safety crime case, it may send personnel to inquire about or review the relevant case materials. If it considers that the case should be transferred, it shall issue a prosecutorial opinion. The emergency management department shall transfer the case to the public security organ within three days from the date of receiving the prosecutorial opinion, and send a copy of the case transfer letter to the people's procuratorate.

Article 18 The people's procuratorate shall, in accordance with the law, approve the arrest of and initiate a public prosecution against criminal suspects who meet the conditions for arrest and prosecution.

For cases in which the people's procuratorate decides not to prosecute, it shall, within three days from the date of making the decision, serve the decision not to prosecute on the public security organ and the emergency management department. If administrative legal liability should be pursued according to law, prosecutorial opinions may also be made at the same time, and the emergency management department shall be requested to promptly report the handling situation.

Chapter III Case Transfer and Legal Supervision in Accident Investigation

Article 19 The public security organ with jurisdiction at the place where the accident occurred shall, based on the circumstances of the accident, file a case and investigate if a work safety crime is suspected, in accordance with the law.

Article 20 If a suspected work safety crime is discovered during the accident investigation, the accident investigation team or the fire protection agency responsible for fire investigation shall promptly transfer the relevant materials or copies thereof to the public security organ with jurisdiction for handling according to law.

During the accident investigation, the accident investigation team or the fire protection agency responsible for fire investigation may hold special meetings to inform the public security organ with jurisdiction of the progress of the accident investigation.

If the public security organ with jurisdiction files a case and investigates a suspected work safety crime case, it shall, within three days, send a copy of the decision to file the case to the emergency management department and people's procuratorate at the same level, as well as to the emergency management department that organized the accident investigation.

Article 21 For suspected work safety crime cases with significant social impact, higher-level public security organs shall strengthen guidance and supervision by means such as listing for supervision and dispatching personnel to participate. When necessary, they may directly organize the handling of the case in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 22 If the emergency management department organizing the accident investigation, the public security organ at the same level, and the people's procuratorate have disagreements on the facts, nature determination, evidence acceptance, application of law, and accountability for suspected work safety crime cases, they shall strengthen coordination and communication. When necessary, they may seek opinions from the people's court on issues such as the application of law.

Article 23 In cases involving the death of one or more persons, if an investigation is conducted in accordance with the law and a written investigation conclusion is made that the case is not a production safety accident or a production safety liability accident, the emergency management department shall promptly send a copy of that investigation conclusion to the supervisory organ, public security organ, and people's procuratorate at the same level.

Chapter IV Collection and Use of Evidence

Article 24 In the course of investigating illegal acts, the relevant emergency management department shall comprehensively collect and properly preserve evidentiary materials. For traces and physical evidence that are easily lost, measures shall be taken to extract and fix them; for items involved in the case that are seized, an inventory of the items involved shall be truthfully filled in and handled in accordance with relevant state regulations; for items involved in the case that require inspection or appraisal, they shall be inspected or appraised by statutory inspection or appraisal institutions, and an inspection report or expert opinion shall be issued.

In the course of accident investigation, the relevant departments shall, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations or the arrangements of the accident investigation team, collect and preserve relevant evidentiary materials as provided in the preceding paragraph.

Article 25 Physical evidence, documentary evidence, audio-visual materials, electronic data, inspection reports, expert opinions, inspection records, examination records, and other evidentiary materials lawfully collected and produced in the course of investigating illegal acts or accident investigations, as well as accident investigation reports approved in accordance with the law, may be used as evidence in criminal proceedings.

The accident investigation report submitted by the accident investigation team in accordance with relevant provisions shall be signed by its members. If not signed, it shall be corrected or a reasonable explanation shall be provided.

Article 26 If a party, defense counsel, or litigation representative raises an objection to an inspection report, expert opinion, inspection record, or examination record and applies for a new inspection, appraisal, inspection, or examination, reasons shall be stated. If the people's court finds it necessary after trial, it shall grant the application. If the people's court grants the application for a new appraisal, it shall promptly commission the appraisal and notify the people's procuratorate, the party, defense counsel, or litigation representative of the appraisal opinion; alternatively, the public security organ may conduct a new inspection, appraisal, inspection, or examination on its own or commission a relevant institution to do so.

Chapter V Collaboration Mechanisms

Article 27 Emergency management departments, public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts at all levels shall establish a long-term working mechanism for the connection between administrative law enforcement and criminal justice in work safety. They shall designate the lead unit and contact person of their respective units and strengthen daily communication and collaboration. They shall hold regular joint meetings to coordinate and resolve important issues and clarify the matters agreed upon in the form of meeting minutes.

The emergency management departments, public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall regularly, on an annual basis, jointly notify information on the transfer, filing, approval of arrest, prosecution, and judgment results of suspected work safety crime cases within their respective jurisdictions.

Article 28 For major, difficult, or complex cases, emergency management departments may consult public security organs or people's procuratorates on issues such as the standards for criminal case filing and prosecution, and the fixation and preservation of evidence; public security organs or people's procuratorates may consult emergency management departments on professional issues in case handling. The consulted authority shall respond promptly; for written consultations, a written response shall be given within seven days.

Article 29 The people's court shall, after the judgment or ruling of a relevant case becomes effective, promptly publish the judgment or ruling on the internet in accordance with regulations. If a professional prohibition measure is imposed, the judgment or ruling shall be served within 10 days after the judgment or ruling becomes effective to the county-level emergency management department and public security organ of the place where the offender resides, with a copy sent to the county-level people's procuratorate of the place where the offender resides. If the offender has the status of a state functionary, the judgment or ruling shall be served to the offender's original work unit.

Article 30 If a people's procuratorate or people's court finds that a relevant production or business unit has problems in ensuring work safety, or that a relevant department has illegal or improper circumstances in performing its work safety supervision and management duties, it may issue a procuratorial recommendation or judicial recommendation. The relevant production or business unit or relevant department shall promptly handle the matter in accordance with regulations and provide a written feedback on the handling situation to the people's procuratorate or people's court that issued the recommendation.

Article 31 Emergency management departments, public security organs, and people's procuratorates at all levels shall use information technology means to gradually realize online transfer, online acceptance, and online supervision of suspected work safety crime cases.

Chapter VI Supplementary Provisions

Article 32 The emergency management departments, public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate implementation measures based on the actual circumstances of their respective regions.

Article 33 These Measures shall take effect as of the date of issuance.
